text:
alex: heads up — after last night's gpu-operator bump we started seeing a few clusters with GPUs in NotReady and a bunch of Pending pods. noticed in eu-west-1 first :frowning:
maria: saw it too. pods are stuck with message 'NoGPUAvailable' and device-plugin logs show registration failures.
chris: throwing logs here — device-plugin on node-12 repeatedly failing probe:
```
I0716 03:12:11.452123   12345 manager.go:200] probing device plugin
E0716 03:12:11.452145   12345 plugin.go:78] driver probe failed: kernel module mismatch: expected 525.x, running 530.x
E0716 03:12:11.452169   12345 plugin.go:92] deviceplugin registration aborted
```
sophia: that's the kernel-module vs driver version mismatch we've seen before after auto-kernel updates on some hosts.
raj: yeah our new gpu-operator manifest changed the driver install order (prePull -> activate modules) and if node had newer kernel the DKMS build wasn't getting triggered early enough.
alex: confirmed. the problematic nodes show kernel upgrades during out-of-band reboots last night. nova/packer image refresh rolled some nodes with 6.1 kernels.
maria: immediate mitigation: cordon + drain the affected nodes and force them into the older driver daemonset by applying rollback taint? or do we roll back operator?
chris: we did a soft-rollout: reverted gpu-operator image to previous tag in canary pool (eu-west-1a) and restarted driver-daemonset there. canary looked ok.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy eu-west-1a gpu-operator:v2.1.3 -> v2.1.2 succeeded (3/3 pods ready) :white_check_mark:
raj: but we still have ~18 nodes across eu-west-1b/c with mismatched kernels. draining will cause capacity pressure and some training jobs will OOM or timeout. cost impact if we scale up temporarily.
alex: agreed. options:
- rollback operator globally (fast but noisy)
- patch operator to defer module activation until after DKMS build completes (safer)
- add a short-lived scheduling exception to avoid re-scheduling GPU jobs to affected nodes
maria: patching will take a couple hours to QA. rollback global could be done in 20-30m. which do we prefer?
chris: do rollback first for safety, then patch. we should also add a k8s mutating webhook to annotate nodes with kernel/driver mismatch to prevent scheduling until fixed.
sophia: rolling back now will spike short-term cost due to forced reprovisioning? but less than failing jobs. +1 for rollback then patch.
alex: ok i'm executing rollback and adding a temporary cluster-wide taint to keep new GPU pods from landing on suspect nodes.
```
# rollback gpu-operator
kubectl -n gpu-system set image deploy/gpu-operator gpu-operator=redwood/gpu-operator:v2.1.2
kubectl rollout status deploy/gpu-operator -n gpu-system

# taint suspect nodes
kubectl taint nodes node-12 node-18 gpu.mismatch=true:NoSchedule
```
infra-bot: rollback initiated by alex at 2025-07-16T03:34:12Z; watchlist: eu-west-1. Alerts suppressed for 30m.
maria: after rollback driver daemonset restarted cleanly on canary and device plugin registered. tracking patch PR: https://git.redwood.company/p/gpu-operator/merge-requests/412
raj: note for oncall: need a follow-up runbook item — when kernel updates happen, ensure DKMS build hook runs before operator driver activation. also consider adding a preflight check in the operator that compares host kernel with driver target and delays rollout if mismatch detected.
alex: opened incident ticket INC-2025-074 and will schedule a retro postmortem tomorrow. for now I'm running a small script to list nodes with mismatches and drain them in waves to avoid capacity cliffs.
```
# find mismatched nodes
kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion}\n{end}' | grep '6.1\|5.15'

# drain loop (throttle)
for n in $(cat mismatched-nodes.txt); do
  kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
  sleep 300
done
```
chris: also flagging that some regions (apac) have constrained spare GPU capacity; if we start wave drains there we might exceed our reserved capacity and incur burst pricing. keep eu-west first.
sophia: documented interim communication for customers with long-running jobs. ops-sig will post on status.redwood if any customer impact appears.
maria: will follow up with a short postmortem draft after retro. thanks team for quick reaction :heart:
alex: thanks — monitoring closely. once patch merged we'll schedule controlled rollout and add preflight check to operator release notes.
